scope: Two cfg(test) fixture constructor boundaries and their matching owning finish receivers. No production behavior, source guard, authority, test body, stack limit or deadline change.

evidence.prior_one_inner_box: a671 already contains Box::pin(preregistered()).await. Root's actual native execution still failed all thirteen common Panel/Host cases with stack-overflow diagnostics.

decisions.before: async fn returning Result<Self>; only the inner preregistered future is boxed.
decisions.after: Ordinary private fn returning an opaque Future whose concrete representation is Pin<Box<the same async move body>>, with Result<Box<Self>> output.
decisions.purpose: Avoid embedding/moving the full completed future and its by-value fixture result in all higher-level caller futures. Keep original preregistration, retention-before-primary sequence, evidence, original owners and error propagation.

decisions.before: async fn returning Result<Self>, destructuring PanelFixture by value then holding HostFixture by value.
decisions.after: The same opaque pinned boxed future shape and Result<Box<Self>> output; move every field once out of the owned Box<PanelFixture> and construct Box<HostFixture> at the original Self-construction point.
decisions.purpose: Keep the large fixture result behind one owning pointer for the ten Host-derived cases, without boxing individual owner fields or editing test bodies.

decisions.after: Owning Box<Self> receiver; Host retains mut. Bodies are byte-identical.
decisions.purpose: Consume the same fixture and every original owner in the exact existing explicit order without moving the full fixture back into a by-value finish future.

owner_and_lifetime_review.eager_allocation_difference: The fixture future is now allocated when the helper is called. Its original business body and original I/O still start only when that future is polled. This is test memory representation, not a new authorization or operation.
owner_and_lifetime_review.limits: Box::pin and Box::new can still create temporary values; the Host owned Box destructure still moves fields. Native compilation, run behavior and any remaining stack pressure require the original validation gate.
